'''Derek Roy Taunt''' (16 November 1917<sup>[[#Notes|(Note 1)]]</sup> &ndash; 15 July 2004) was a British [[mathematician]] who worked as a [[Cryptanalysis|codebreaker]] during [[World War II]] at [[Bletchley Park]].

Taunt attended [[Enfield Grammar School|Enfield Grammar]], then the [[City of London School]].<ref name="telegraph">{{cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1467625/Derek-Taunt.html|title=Obituary: Derek Taunt|date=23 July 2004|newspaper=The Telegraph}}</ref> He studied mathematics at [[Jesus College, Cambridge|Jesus College]], [[University of Cambridge|Cambridge]] between 1936 and 1939.<ref name="taunt">Derek Taunt, ''Hut 6 From the Inside'', pp. 77-93 in ''Action this Day'', edited by Ralph Erskine and Michael Smith, 2001, {{ISBN|0-593-04982-9}}</ref> He was accepted as a research student by [[G. H. Hardy]], but this was postponed by the outbreak of World War II. Taunt registered with the Joint Recruiting Board, and was initially allocated to work on [[ballistics]] at Kemnal Manor in [[Chislehurst]], preparing range tables for new weapons. Finding that the task required only trivial mathematics ("more like advanced arithmetic than real mathematics"<ref name="taunt"/>), he sought more appropriate work.

In August 1941 he was moved to Bletchley Park and assigned to [[Hut 6]], the section in charge of decrypting German Army and Air Force [[Enigma (machine)|Enigma]] signals. While there, he was best man at the marriage of co-workers [[Bob Roseveare]] and Ione Jay.

After his wartime work, he returned to Cambridge, and worked on [[group theory]]. He was a research student (1945), wrote a doctoral dissertation under [[Philip Hall]], won a [[Smith's Prize]] in 1949, and was a Lecturer from 1949 with the honorific title of 'Cayley Lecturer' from 1965 until retirement in 1982. As a Fellow of [[Jesus College, Cambridge|Jesus College]] he was at various times a director of studies, tutor, bursar, and from 1979 to 1982 was president.  In 1982 he became emeritus Fellow, "with most of the privileges and none of the duties of a Fellow." His doctoral students include [[Roger Carter (mathematician)|Roger Carter]].

On 18 December 1952 Taunt was elected a member of the [[London Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/330/330_09.html Deaths: DEREK TAUNT, LMS Newsletter, London Mathematical Society] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20140217151614/http://newsletter.lms.ac.uk/330/330_09.html |date=2014-02-17 }}</ref> He was married to the English artist [[Angela Verren]] with whom he had three children.<ref name="BuckmanVol2">{{cite book|author=David Buckman|publisher=Art Dictionaries Ltd|year=2006|title=Artists in Britain Since 1945 Vol 2, M to Z |isbn=0-953260-95-X}}</ref>

==Notes==
1. The obituary published in the Telegraph gives his birth date as the 16th,<ref name="telegraph"/> while that in the 2004 Jesus College Annual Report incorrectly records it as the 17th.<ref name="jesus">[http://www.jesus.cam.ac.uk/alumni/publications/Annual%20Report%202004.pdf Jesus College Annual Report for 2004] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060630001411/http://www.jesus.cam.ac.uk/alumni/publications/Annual%20Report%202004.pdf |date=2006-06-30 }}, p. 83-85</ref> GRO death index gives it as the 16th.

2. Derek Taunt gives an account of his war work in: {{cite book  | first1 = F.H. | last1 = Hinsley | first2 = Alan | last2 = Stripp |title = Codebreakers: The inside story of Bletchley Park | publisher = [[OUP]] | year = 1994 | isbn = 0-19-285304-X | chapter = 13: Hut 6 1941-1945}}
